title: Mansaf – Lamb with Jameed Yogurt Sauce
description: Mansaf is a traditional Jordanian Arabic dish made with tender lamb cooked in aromatic spices and served over rice with a rich fermented jameed yogurt sauce. It is a celebratory dish known for its deep flavor and communal presentation.

ingredients.title: For the Lamb
items: 2 kg lamb shoulder or leg, bone-in, cut into large chunks

ingredients.title: For the Jameed (Yogurt) Sauce
items: 2 cups jameed (dried fermented yogurt) OR thick Greek yogurt

ingredients.title: For the Rice
items: 3 cups long-grain basmati rice, soaked 30 minutes

ingredients.title: For Garnish
items: 1/2 cup toasted slivered almonds or pine nuts

instruction.title: Instructions
steps:
1. Cook the Lamb:
• Place lamb, onions, garlic, spices, and water in a large pot.
• Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer 1.5–2 hours until tender.
• Skim impurities from the surface.
• Remove lamb and strain broth for later use.

2. Prepare the Jameed/Yogurt Sauce:
• Soak jameed if using dried, then blend until smooth.
• In a saucepan, combine jameed or yogurt with 2 cups lamb broth.
• Cook on low heat, stirring constantly to prevent curdling.
• Add ghee and season with salt.
• Simmer until thick and creamy.

3. Cook the Rice:
• Heat ghee and lightly toast soaked rice for 2–3 minutes.
• Add 4 cups lamb broth and salt.
• Bring to boil, reduce heat, cover, and simmer 12–15 minutes until fluffy.

4. Assemble the Mansaf:
• Spread flatbread on a large platter (optional traditional base).
• Layer rice, then lamb pieces on top.
• Pour warm jameed sauce generously over everything.
• Garnish with toasted nuts and parsley.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve on a large communal platter for traditional dining
Pair with Arabic salad or pickles
Enjoy with warm flatbread (shrak or pita)
Serve with extra jameed sauce on the side

chefTips: Use bone-in lamb for deeper, richer flavor.
Authentic jameed gives the most traditional taste; yogurt is a substitute.
Rinse rice well for fluffy, separated grains.
Serve on a large copper or decorative platter for presentation impact.
